concept.name: Absorption
concept.definition: A market condition in which sustained aggressive market orders hit a price level but fail to move it, because resting limit orders repeatedly fill the incoming flow. Heavy traded volume with little or no price progress is the footprint signature of a large passive participant absorbing the aggressive side.
concept.intuition: It is like waves breaking against a seawall: the market orders keep arriving, but a wall of limit orders soaks them up and price refuses to budge.
concept.mechanics: Detected on footprint/tape as high bid- or ask-side volume at a level combined with stalled price (e.g., bearish candles with positive delta, or iceberg-style reloading of the displayed quote); iceberg orders are a formal special case in which a hidden-size limit order absorbs flow while displaying only a tip.
concept.failure_modes: Absorption is identifiable only after the fact at the level, and the absorbing side can pull its liquidity at any moment; apparent absorption can also be ordinary two-sided interest with no single large participant behind it.
concept.misconceptions: Absorption does not guarantee reversal — if the absorbing limit orders are eventually consumed, price breaks violently through the level; absorption marks a battle, not its outcome.
concept.example: Sellers hit the bid at 4,500 with 12,000 contracts over ten minutes yet price never trades below 4,499.75; the stalling on heavy sell-side volume marks absorption by passive buyers.
